smells.finding: fit_track_evolution (lines 225-319, ~95 lines) does FE-slope fit, per-weekend spline fit, sigma calc, and wide-sigma derivation in one function. It stays a single cohesive concern (fit the whole latent) and the loop body is not separable without adding indirection for a one-call-site helper, so this is a minor, non-blocking observation, not a rewrite demand.

_connect_readonly (3-line sqlite mode=ro URI helper) is copy-pasted verbatim from frame.py (g1) into layer2_evolution.py (lines 123-125) rather than shared from a common util. Each module reads a different DB (physics_estimates.db vs damage_integrals.db) so a shared helper would need a tiny refactor; flagging as a minor, non-blocking cleanup candidate for Admiral/Triage, not overriding since no documented standard mandates per-module duplication (only observed precedent, one prior instance).

(year, gp_name) tuple keys recur across coverage/splines/ctl_ref/ctl_span/sigma dicts, but they are genuinely the natural composite key for a per-weekend fit and are encapsulated behind TrackEvolutionFit + latent_at/apply_track_evolution; not a clump forcing callers to know the pieces separately.

Nothing built ahead of need: apply_track_evolution/loo_earns_keep/orthogonality_vs_season are all exercised by the tests and are exactly what the handoff's honest-verdict deliverable requires; no unused hooks or extension points.
The module docstring and EARNS_KEEP_VERDICT constant are long (~120 lines of prose) relative to the code.
